name: King of Goiim in Gilgal
overview: The King of Goiim in Gilgal was a male ruler identified as one of thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of the Promised Land. His tribal affiliation and additional personal details are not recorded in Scripture. He is known primarily through his defeat as listed in the book of Joshua.
namesAndTitles: This individual is referred to by the title 'King of Goiim in Gilgal,' which is a straightforward designation without a special Hebrew or Greek meaning provided. The title indicates his kingship over the Goiim in the city of Gilgal, as noted in Joshua 12:23.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for this king beyond his identification as one of the defeated rulers in Joshua 12:23.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Goiim in Gilgal holds significance as a representative of the Canaanite kings who opposed God's appointed leader, Joshua, during Israel's conquest of the land promised to Abraham's descendants. His defeat underscores God's faithfulness in granting Israel victory over its enemies, fulfilling His covenant promises. This king's mention highlights the comprehensive nature of Joshua's campaign and the divine mandate behind it.
